newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yugansk says 96 pre-tax loss 299 bln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Yugansk says 96 pre-tax loss 299 bln rbls.

text.p: Russia's OAO Yuganskneftegaz crude oil producer said on Monday it swung into a 1996 pre-tax loss to Russian accruals-based accounting standards of 299 billion roubles from a 1.26 trillion rouble pre-tax profit in 1995.
On a cash basis it had a pre-tax profit of 245 billion roubles in 1996, it said in a statement.
NOTE - Figures in billion roubles. Accruals basis.
Vertically integrated oil group NK YUKOS has a controlling stake in Yuganskneftegaz. Other big shareholders are CS First Boston and Crawford Holdings.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
Year-on-year consumer price inflation rate in December 1996 was 21.8 percent after 131 percent in December 1995 and 215 percent in December 1994.
